title: Automated Regression for Logistics Routing Agents
business: Logistics companies managing automated delivery dispatch agents.
problem: Agents occasionally misinterpret complex delivery constraints, leading to costly manual rerouting and delayed shipments.
solution: Implement an evaluation loop that runs representative delivery scenarios through a deterministic test harness, scoring agent trace outcomes against expected constraints and feeding failures back into prompt refinement.
steps: Define a suite of representative delivery scenarios as deterministic ScriptedModel sequences.
Execute agent runs within the testing harness to capture normalized interaction traces.
Compare agent tool-use outputs against expected delivery constraints using assertion logic.
Identify failed traces where agents violated routing rules or failed to call required tools.
Update system prompts or tool definitions based on the specific failure patterns identified in the traces.
outcome: Higher reliability in complex routing decisions and reduced manual intervention for edge-case delivery scenarios.
limitation: The evaluation loop relies on deterministic scripting; it cannot simulate the stochastic nature of real-world traffic or unpredictable API latency, requiring separate integration testing.

diagram.title: Agent Evaluation Loop Process
diagram.description: The cycle of testing agent logic against defined scenarios and using the results to improve agent performance.

code.content:
from agents.testing import ScriptedModel, assistant_message
# Define a deterministic scenario for the routing agent
model = ScriptedModel([[assistant_message("Route: Zone A to Zone B")]])
# The agent uses this model to simulate a specific routing decision
agent = Agent(name="Router", model=model)
# Run the agent and assert the outcome matches the expected routing constraint
result = await Runner.run(agent, "Optimize route", run_config=RunConfig(tracing_disabled=True))
assert result.final_output == "Route: Zone A to Zone B" # Validates agent logic
code.explanation: This code maps to the business scenario by using ScriptedModel to enforce a specific, repeatable routing decision for the agent, allowing the developer to verify if the agent correctly follows the routing constraints.
